atoms.b:
Different materials behave ((++differently in_the_same_way)) around electricity.
Certain materials, such as copper, ((++conduct insulate)) electricity. This means that they allow electricity to flow through them.

instruction.text: Now, select the material that does not conduct electricity.

feedback.end: Wires are wrapped in plastic because plastic is an insulator. This allows us to touch wires without being electricuted.

atoms.b: Other materials, such as plastic, do not conduct electricity. These materials are called ((conductors ++insulators)).

atoms.a: Materials can be conductors or insulators.
Only solids and liquids can be conductors.

feedback.end: Solids, liquids and gases can all be conductors.

atoms.a: Insulators, such as plastics, are very important because we can use them to protect ourselves from dangerous electric shocks.

instruction.text: Sort the following items into the correct categories.

hint.text: Select the images to hear what they are.

feedback.end: Water can conduct electricity, which is why it is dangerous to use electrical appliances in the bathroom, where they might get wet.
